## 2026-07-15 18:38 UTC-05:00 · round-close · recommender
P5 FIXED: rankSources divided mg by mcg. All 19 boron candidates read adequacy 1.0000 — the 0.6 keystone was a CONSTANT, so ranking collapsed to breadth+price. Silver read 0.0001 (truth 0.10). Converter promoted to core/units.ts because boundaries forbids state→state.
  ↳ [2026-07-15 18:42 CDT] Recommender / P5 — unit reconciliation · Our "best source of X" ranker scores each product 60% on "does it give you enough", and to work that out it divided the product's amount by Wallach's target. Trouble: those two numbers don't always use the same unit. For boron, Wallach's target is in milligrams while every product lists it in micrograms — a 1000x difference — so the maths said every single one of the 19 boron products delivered 100% of the target. All 19 scored identically on the most important term, which means it contributed NOTHING and the ranking quietly fell back to "how many nutrients does it have" plus price. Silver had the same bug backwards and scored ~0. Fixed by converting both numbers to a common unit before dividing, exactly the way the coverage engine has always done it 20 lines away. Also made it refuse to guess: hand it a target without telling it the unit and it now falls back to the honest proxy and SAYS so, rather than assuming the units happen to match. · MEASURED, real data, before vs after — BORON (target 9.2 mg, candidates in mcg): all 19 candidates read adequacy 1.0000 pre-fix; post-fix they spread 0.0543 (bone-building-formula, 500 mcg) → 0.5435 (xeratest, 5000 mcg). SILVER (target 400 mcg, candidates in mg): colloidal-silver 0.0001 → 0.1000; ultimate-colloidal-silver 0.0000 → 0.0325 — the 0.0001→0.10 matches the handoff's predicted truth EXACTLY. SCOPE PINNED FIRST: of the 34 essentials carrying BOTH a numeric target and vault candidates, exactly 2 mismatch (boron mg-vs-mcg, silver mcg-vs-mg); the other 32 agree — so this was never a broad corruption, it was two nutrients, precisely as flagged. · NEW dashboard/assets/js/src/core/units.ts (toMg + IU_TO_MG promoted out of state/coverage.ts). WHY A NEW FILE, not a copy: `eslint-plugin-boundaries` allows `state → core` ONLY, so state/recommender.ts CANNOT import state/coverage.ts. The two options were duplicate the converter (R3 violation — one source per fact) or promote it. THE LAYER RULE WAS RIGHT and picked the fix for us. Both state modules now share one conversion truth. · state/recommender.ts — rankSources gains a 3rd param `targetUnit`; `useTarget` now requires that the target's unit RECONCILES with the candidates' into the same family (probed via toMg(1, unit) which reports 'mg' | 'iu'); adequacy converts BOTH sides before dividing. FAIL-SAFE not fail-quiet: a target with no unit, or a cross-family clash (IU target vs mg candidates), falls back to the potency proxy and reports adequacyIsTarget:false rather than guessing. Wrong-but-plausible is the failure mode this codebase exists to refuse. · views/knowledge-products.ts — NEW targetUnitOf() beside targetLowOf(); the call site now passes the unit so it travels WITH the number. · ★ THE TELL: state/coverage.ts:656 + :776 have ALWAYS done this correctly (`const low = isIU ? lowRaw : toMg(lowRaw, target.unit).v`) — converting both delivery and target. design-system.css's seal was fingerprinted over this machine's CRLF bytes — a sequence git has never stored — so the critical gate was green only here and would RED on any fresh clone as if the sealed file were tampered with. Now LF-normalized like every other seal. Re-sealed.
  ↳ The design system's stylesheet is "sealed" — we store a fingerprint of it so that if anyone tampers with it, a check goes red. But the fingerprint had been taken of the file as it sits on THIS machine, with Windows line endings, while git stores the file with Unix line endings. So the fingerprint described a version of the file git has never stored. The check passed here and nowhere else: anyone cloning the repo fresh would get a CRITICAL red screaming that a sealed file had been tampered with, when nothing had. Fixed by fingerprinting the content in a line-ending-independent way — which is what every other sealed file in the project already did. This one was the only holdout. THE SHARPEST STATEMENT OF THE BUG: the golden recorded 37c338b7..., the sha256 of the 47,691-byte CRLF working tree. The committed blob is 46,563 bytes, LF, sha256 037d0e3e.... `git ls-files --eol` says `i/lf w/crlf`, and core.autocrlf=input does not convert on checkout. So the seal was anchored to bytes that exist on exactly one disk in the world. WHAT WAS FIXED - NEW _lf_file_hash() beside _file_hash() in tools/invariants.py — sha256 of LF-normalized content, matching corpus_seal/catalog_seal/products_seal's lf_sha256(). - check_design_system_hash_integrity switched to it (call site 558 ONLY). - _file_hash DELIBERATELY LEFT RAW. It has a live second caller at line 1968: the graphics gate. eden/graphics/*.jpg are marked `binary` in .gitattributes, git never EOL-converts them, and raw bytes ARE the truth there — LF-normalizing a JPEG's hash would corrupt that seal. Changing _file_hash globally was the obvious move and would have been wrong. - The golden re-sealed 37c338b7... -> 037d0e3e.... THE CSS CONTENT WAS NOT TOUCHED: `git diff --quiet design-system.css` is clean, and the new golden EQUALS the raw sha256 of the committed blob. The seal now anchors to bytes git actually stores. - .gitattributes: dashboard/assets/styles/*.css + *.golden.sha256 pinned `text eol=lf`. This is DEFENCE IN DEPTH, not the fix — the gate is now EOL-agnostic regardless. It stops the working tree diverging from the blob again. - An EOL-aware hint added to the failure message: if the golden matches the file's RAW hash but not its LF hash, the message now says so explicitly ("a stale raw-byte seal, NOT a content edit"). A bare "hash mismatch" on a sealed canonical reads as tampering, and that misdiagnosis is expensive. - truth_anchor prose corrected. It said "raw-byte SHA-256" — accurate, and itself the defect being described. R9 — THE REFINEMENT SHIPS WITH ITS PROOF (tools/test_design_system_gates.py, 3 new cases) - eol_agnostic: the same content under LF and CRLF hashes identically AND equals the golden. This is the case the pre-fix gate fails. - content_edit_still_caught: THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the load-bearing half. A one-byte NON-EOL edit must STILL move the digest. Without it, "ignores line endings" could be satisfied by a function that ignores everything. A test that cannot reproduce the bug it guards proves nothing. - file_hash_still_raw: the raw hasher must still SEE an EOL difference, proving the split did not drift the binary graphics seal. - REPAIRED IN THE SAME PATCH: the pre-existing forged_hash_mismatch case patched inv._file_hash — which the fixed gate no longer calls. Graphics raw-hashing is correct by construction. design-system was the sole holdout — so the fix adopts the existing pattern, it does not invent one. HONEST RED: invariants finished 68/69. design_system_write_protection is RED BY DESIGN — it anchors the working golden to `git show HEAD:<golden>` and reds while a golden is changed-but-uncommitted. That is the gate doing its job: it exists to catch an agent re-sealing SILENTLY, and a legitimate re-seal is supposed to be a visible, deliberate commit. It clears the moment this commit lands. Reported, not hidden, and not baselined. METHOD: found by a 37-agent adversarial audit (631 tool calls). We had a gate proving every target on screen traces back to a claim. So the chain ran airtight from the screen back to the claim, and then just stopped. I proved it rather than argued it: a planted 10x sodium fabrication (3,300 -> 33,000 mg) passed the ENTIRE board green — including `amounts_wallach_only` reporting "all 38 numeric coverage target(s) trace to a Wallach dose claim AND recompute exactly from its documented transform chain (R2 clean)" — while the claim's own verbatim still read "3,300 mg". That is the cornerstone of this whole project, and it had a hole in it. The new gate reads Wallach's printed number and compares. On its first run it found a real defect (below), which is now fixed. TECHNICAL RECORD NEW INVARIANT `dose_amount_in_verbatim` (critical). Every claim's structured dose.amount must be literally present in that claim's OWN verbatim: unit-adjacent, scoped to the claim's own table row, and at the correct column index where dose.for_condition names one. Truth anchor: the claim's verbatim bytes, which corpus_integrity independently pins to the sealed book .txt. The three R2 gates now compose — R5/corpus_integrity proves the quote is the book's, this proves the number is the quote's, amounts_wallach_only proves the target is the number's. THE DESIGN WAS ATTACKED BEFORE IT SHIPPED, AND BROKEN THREE WAYS. All three are closed and pinned as tests: 1. CROSS-ROW BLEED. 72 of 86 claims accepted a fabrication drawn from their own verbatim, because 37 of 86 spans name more than one nutrient — the mined span routinely carries the NEXT table row. Closed by slicing the span on nutrient-NAME boundaries. 2. UNIT SWAP (the dangerous one). LETS-000048 choline 600 mg re-tagged `mcg` — a 1000x UNDER-dose — passed green, because chromium's row in the same span reads "300 to 600 mcg". This is the invisible failure mode: an understated target silently marks a user COVERED when they are not. LETS-000073 vitamin C mg -> IU passed off vitamin D's row (dimensionally nonsense, still certified). Critically, the spec's OWN proposed fix — "require the unit adjacent to the matched amount" — does NOT close this: 600 is adjacent to mg AND to mcg. Anyone implementing the documented remedy would have believed the axis closed while the live 1000x hole remained. Only row identity closes it. 3. IN-ROW COLUMN BLEED. The Let's Play Doctor base-line table prints NAME | RDA | true-supplement-need | pharmacologic, and dose.amount is column 1. So sodium 3,300 -> its own RDA 1,100 is a 3x understatement that presence-checking can never see. Closed by indexing the column positionally where for_condition declares it. Verified against real data: 30 rows column-checked, ZERO false-fires. WHAT SHAPED THE SCOPING. Row slicing keys on nutrient-name boundaries, NOT newlines, because table rows are sometimes space-joined on one line while prose is hard-wrapped mid-phrase. The discriminator is a follow-test: a name heads a table row iff a number (or a "?" placeholder) follows it, optionally past a form parenthetical ("Vitamin A (retinol) 2,500 IU"). In prose a name is followed by a word ("chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg"), which fails the test and leaves the span whole. This matters: an early newline-splitting design severed "Twenty to 30 mg ... for\ngermanium." from its own subject and RED-boarded a perfectly good claim. Every ambiguous path falls back to the FULL span — scoping may only ever tighten, never invent a narrower window that hides a mismatch. ## 2026-07-14 12:10 UTC-05:00 · incident · design-system
Reduced-motion block was strobing the app at ~100Hz for the users who asked for LESS motion — capped duration but never iteration-count; 7 painted offenders measured, fixed in one line, gated by a new render probe + proven with a negative test
  ↳ Anyone whose computer is set to "reduce motion" was getting a strobing page instead of a calm one — the exact opposite of what they asked for. The rule that was supposed to quiet our animations only capped how LONG each loop lasts, never how MANY times it repeats. So a 10-second loop told to take 0.01 seconds did not stop; it ran a hundred times per second. Seven things on screen were flashing. The fix is one line. The more important part is the new probe that makes it impossible to reintroduce — this bug was invisible to every gate we had, because the CSS said the right thing and did the opposite, so reading the code could never have caught it. Only measuring the real browser could. CAUSE. design-system.css:307-318, the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block, set `animation-duration: 0.01s !important` and `transition-duration: 0.01s !important` — and never set `animation-iteration-count`. Capping duration does not stop an `infinite` animation; it accelerates it 1000x. Measured headless (puppeteer, emulateMediaFeatures prefers-reduced-motion=reduce, verified honored by the browser): 7 PAINTED offenders at ~100Hz — ds-scan-sweep on .ds-scan-line (the worst: ramps opacity 0->0.35 while sweeping top from -3% to 103% across .essentials-host), ds-numeric-glow on .coverage-stat__num (the hero 13/90), ds-stat-pulse on .coverage-stat::before, ds-travel-top/-bottom on .coverage-hero::before/::after, and ds-pulse-animate on both .topbar__ask-dot and .topbar__workspace-tag::before. WCAG 2.3.1 puts the flash threshold at 3/sec. Honest severity: the scan-line is a real flash hazard (position + opacity over a large host); the other six are luminance shimmers on small or soft elements — genuinely wrong, not the same class. I am not going to inflate them. FIX. One declaration — `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` — inside the same block. design-system.css is SEALED; user sign-off is Luneth 2026-07-14 ("1. Yes"). Golden re-sealed cdf0ebd4... -> 37c338b7..., with the CSS written BEFORE the golden so design_system_write_protection's mtime rule (css_mtime > seal_mtime + 1 = violation) holds.   ↳ This is the second half of the "Ask Wallach" search: making it actually understand how people type. Before, you had to type the exact name; now the search knows Wallach's own everyday words for things — so "blood sugar" brings up Diabetes, "quicksilver" brings up Mercury, "b12" brings up Cobalt, "climate" brings up Carbon — and each result quietly notes which word matched ("via 'blood sugar'"). It also ranks results sensibly and, importantly, it will NOT show the homosexuality/intersex material unless someone explicitly searches those words — that content stays in the Explore index only. Luneth signed it off. Prototype-only — temporary/knowledge-drawer-prototype.html (gitignored demo; no pillar/artifact/app code touched, board stays 53/53). Data: re-injected CLAIMS carrying the full modern-voice `answer` text (real recall — fixes "sugar cravings", which lived in the answer body I'd dropped in chunk 1) + a resolved SEARCH_ENTITIES synonym table (the 56 search entities → {slug, name, k, syn}); all 56 resolve 1:1 to the browse ESS/CONDS/TOPICS (verified 0 misses), so synonyms attach to real pages. Logic: replaced the crude all-words searchClaims with a tiered-scoring suite. apTier scores a field exact(6) › prefix(5) › word-start(4) › substring(3). nameTier weights the display name ×20, an exact element symbol =100 (so "cr" → Chromium ranks with a name-prefix, tie broken by claim count), slug words ×12. aliasTier weights a synonym ×16 (between name and slug). rankEntities scans ESS/CONDS/TOPICS by name + the SEARCH_ENTITIES synonyms, dedups by k:slug taking the max score, and tags synonym-sourced rows with a "via <synonym>" hint. rankClaims scores each claim question(12)/subject(9)/answer_short(6)/answer(4) with per-query-word coverage(+2 each) and a +8 subject-boost when the query hit an entity's name/synonym (so "blood sugar" boosts every diabetes claim). Both replace the old searchAll/searchClaims calls in apRender. Charged-content gate (Luneth's explicit ask): CHARGED = {homosexuality, intersex}. chargedExplicit(q) marks a charged subject "explicitly named" only on a strong match — the entity name exact/prefix OR an EXACT synonym ("gay", "homosexual", "same-sex attraction", "lgbt"…), never an incidental substring. rankEntities filters charged entities out unless explicit; rankClaims skips charged-subject claims unless explicit. Result: "testosterone" and "sexual" no longer pull up homosexuality; "gay"/"homosexual"/"intersex" still do. The Explore tab is EXEMPT (it doesn't use these rankers) and remains the full categorised index. Testosterone/strength reality check: the corpus genuinely has no "increase testosterone / get stronger" content yet — the only "testosterone" hits are incidental mentions inside aromatherapy/cholesterol/homosexuality claims, and sexual_health has just 1 claim. So that's a MINING gap, not a code gap; I did not fake mappings (anti-fakery). Two follow-ups captured for the search-mining phase: (1) proactively mine + tag general-interest lay topics people search — men's-health / strength / vitality with lay synonyms ("increase testosterone", "get stronger", "build muscle", "stamina", "virility") — the ranking machinery is ready and will light up the moment the data is tagged, exactly like "blood sugar" does now; (2) the charged-search-gate becomes doctrine (port to the real search build) + backfill missing synonyms like "lesbian" → homosexuality. Verified with a dedicated headless puppeteer probe driving the REAL global nav()/goCrumb()/trail (not a re-implementation): 12× Calcium⇄Osteoporosis ping-pong → trail never exceeds length 2 (was unbounded); 8 distinct branches → caps at 6 = [Home, Copper, Boron, Iodine, Chromium, Vanadium] with Home preserved, oldest dropped, most-recent kept; the Home crumb resets detail/trail and lands on the Home tab; DOM renders "Home › Calcium › Osteoporosis" with Home first; zero page errors. ## 2026-07-09 01:15 UTC-05:00 · round-close · tools
Phase-G task-zero: built the source-anchored substance triage buffer + its critical substance_triage_accounted gate — park an unmatched substance instead of typo-polluting the registry or dropping it. Board 52/52 (+1 gate); teeth proven by a 6-case negative test.
  ↳ We built the "honest escape hatch" for book mining, which resumes now that Phase G is unlocked. When the books mention a substance our nutrient registry doesn't know yet, it could be one of two things: an OCR typo off a noisy scanned page, or a genuinely-new herb Wallach names. The strict gate (references_resolve) already refuses to let a claim cite an unregistered substance. The danger was at the moment you fix that red board: the lazy move is to force the unmatched name — typo and all — into our pristine registry just to go green. This buffer is a third, legitimate exit: park the substance in a staging file with its source context and leave it out of the claim for now, so the board stays green honestly. Parking is now the LOWER-effort path than cheating, which is what drains the incentive to cheat. A separate accounting gate keeps the parked pile visible so it can't be silently forgotten — it turns RED if a book is ever marked fully-mined while it still has un-reviewed parked substances. NEW eden/tools/substance-triage-buffer.json — staging scaffolding, NOT a pillar, NOT sealed, starts empty (entries: []). Per-entry source context: id (STB-####), raw_name (raw OCR), book_id, locator (page/screenshot), context (surrounding text), claim_id (str|null for backfill), noticed_at, status (pending|resolved|rejected), resolution (required non-empty once terminal). The buffer is NEVER a source of truth — references_resolve never reads it; the single substance registry stays eden/catalog/nutrients.json (no drift). NEW eden/tools/substance_triage.py — the low-friction CLI (this IS the least-resistance mechanism): park / resolve / list / selftest, all writes routed through safe_write.safe_rewrite (§17), same family as mine_batch (incl. a selftest). argv-safe: argparse with required subcommands, nothing mutates on --help or a bare invocation (user-only-tools rule). resolve refuses an empty reason. tools/invariants.py — NEW critical gate check_substance_triage_accounted + registration (52nd invariant). Modeled beat-for-beat on mining_coverage_accounted: pending entries are informational while a book is mining_status:'incomplete', RED the moment that book is flagged 'complete' in mining-coverage.json (teeth at completion, quiet before). Also structural: valid JSON, unique ids, required fields, terminal status carries a non-empty resolution. Bootstrap-safe (missing/empty buffer = pass). Path-override params (buffer_path/coverage_path) make it testable without touching real files. references_resolve left strict/RED and untouched (the WARN softening was rejected in the design chat). Design fidelity: re-compared against the original design transcript with Luneth. Faithful on all agreed points — single trusted registry, strict gate, source-anchored triage buffer, one *_accounted reader, batched resolution against source images, promote real ones + mine_batch backfill, idiomatic not new machinery, built at Phase-G kickoff not before. One confirmed refinement, Model-A→B: the substance is kept OUT of the claim and parked (GREEN board) rather than left in the claim (RED board) — the synthesis the escape-hatch principle requires ("parking beats lying" only holds if parking earns green). Luneth OK'd it explicitly. Verified: build OK (dist 3984.9 KB); invariants 52/52 (was 51/51, +1 new gate, 0 new reds); substance_triage.py selftest PASS; 6-case negative test PASS (pending/incomplete-book→green informational, pending/complete-book→RED teeth, resolved→release green, rejected-with-empty-reason→RED, missing-field→RED, duplicate-id→RED). Render probes N/A — internal tooling, no view/surface touched. Deferred: none for this item. Next: resume Phase-G book mining (task-zero is complete; the strict gate now ships with its relief valve).
